title: Usage event ancestry reconciler and soft-schema coercion
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our usage pipeline is rejecting or dropping ~0.4% of incoming events because callers sometimes send variant payload shapes when a downstream service mutates envelope metadata (trace/parent ids) or forwards batched events with different ancestry headers. This leads to lost signals in billing and telemetry dashboards and noisy alerts during deploys.

Goal: Implement an "ancestry reconciler" at the ingestion gateway that recovers lineage metadata and merges compatible variants of the same logical event, plus introduce a configurable soft-schema-coercion stage to accept slightly divergent shapes with confidence scoring so we can reduce hard rejects while protecting consumers from invalid data. The feature must be toggleable and observable, with a controlled rollout (canary -> global) and a rollback path.

Key ideas:
- Ancestry reconciliation: identify events that share an idempotency key or logical_id and merge envelope-level fields (parent_trace, routed_region, original_timestamp) with last-writer-wins heuristics + tombstone awareness.
- Soft-schema coercion: perform field-level coercion where possible (string->int coercion where numeric patterns present, timestamp parsing, minor key rename mapping). Emit a confidence score for each coerced field; persist original raw payload in archive tier for audit.
- Policy engine: configurable rules per-customer or route (strict, soft, permissive). Default for public routes: soft for up to 1 minute of grouping window.
- Metrics & observability: new metrics for coercion_rate, reconciliation_merge_rate, reconciliation_conflicts, downstream_consumer_errors, and histogram for ingestion_latency_post_reconciliation. Add tracing annotations and sample storage for low-confidence merges.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Accepting coerced data reduces rejects but may change downstream semantics; confidence scores + archiving mitigate this.
- Merging events risks assembling unrelated events if logical keys collide; mitigate with short grouping window and routing-by-source.
- Additional CPU/memory cost at gateway; plan to throttle via admission control and offload heavy work to an async reconciliation worker for large batches.

Success criteria:
- Reduce ingestion hard-reject rate from ~0.4% to <0.05% for targeted routes within the canary cohort.
- No >10% relative increase in 95th percentile ingestion latency for host gateways in canary.
- Consumers report no increase in downstream schema errors and billing reconciliation matches expected within 0.1% for canary customers.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can detect and group events by idempotency/logical_id within a configurable window
Field-level coercion rules applied with confidence scoring and original payload persisted
Canary rollout controls present and telemetry dashboards show coercion_rate and reconciliation_merge_rate
Rollback toggles revert to strict rejects without data loss and archived raw payloads are accessible for audits
comments: 2026-02-19 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage and spike. Reproduced issue with customer dataset (s3://redwood-telemetry/test-cases/ancestry-variants). Observed parent_trace differences when gateway forwarded batched sub-events. Decided to prototype grouping by 'logical_id' + 'source_fingerprint'.

2026-02-25 - Ethan Zhao: Spike complete. Implemented prototype reconciler in local gateway proxy. Performance looks OK for small batches; 95p latency +8% on p50 only. Pushed draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Ancestry+Reconciler+Design

2026-03-01 - Design review notes from Priya Kaur (Product): Prefer explicit confidence field to be stored on event metadata column for downstream filtering. Add 'archive raw' requirement for compliance customers.

2026-03-04 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed coercion rules don't widen attack surface. Recommend restricting coercion for authenticated enterprise routes until review. Marked security_review_required=false but note follow-up for enterprise gating.
2026-03-06 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-gateway/pull/1982 - gateway reconciler + basic coercion rule engine. Needs integration tests for idempotency collision cases.

2026-03-10 - QA (Sofia Nguyen): Found edge case when two events with same logical_id arrive with mutually incompatible nested arrays. Plan: keep strict fallback path that marks conflict and persists both raw payloads, then emit reconciliation_conflicts counter. Added test vectors (s3://redwood-telemetry/test-cases/conflict-vectors).
2026-03-12 - Ethan Zhao: Feature-flag introduced (FF_RECONCILE_SOFT_SCHEMA). Starting canary with 10% of ingestion traffic for 'console' customer routes next week. Monitoring dashboard links below.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 - Spike (done): reproduce, PoC in gateway proxy, perf evaluation
Phase 1 - Core: implement ancestry reconciler + field coercion engine with feature flag and policy layer
Phase 2 - Async offload: large-batch reconciliation worker and admission control for backpressure
Phase 3 - Canary: enable FF for 10% console routes, monitor metrics, iterate
Phase 4 - Gradual rollout: 50% -> 100% with per-customer opt-in for permissive mode
Phase 5 - Post-rollout: add formal audit tooling to query archived raw payloads and integrate with billing reconciler
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False merges due to logical_id collisions. Mitigation: short default grouping window (60s) + source_fingerprint + conflict metric to detect anomalies
Risk: CPU/memory spike at gateway. Mitigation: admission controls, throttle heavy merges, offload to async worker
Risk: Downstream consumers misinterpret coerced fields. Mitigation: include confidence metadata and provide 'strict' per-route mode
Risk: Compliance concerns for enterprise customers. Mitigation: archive raw payloads and add per-customer gating in policy engine
next_steps: Complete integration tests for collision and conflict vectors (assigned to QA)
Merge PR #1982 after address comments from eng-review (deadline 2026-03-16)
Schedule canary on 2026-03-18 and prepare dashboard alerts for regression thresholds
